title: Lettre Tate (mai 66) (Cristaux) : lettre (1966), tapuscrit (s.d.), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: Section 2 of the May 1966 letter to Tate on crystals, at the point where the de Rham cristal DR^1(A/S) of an abelian scheme is identified with the Dieudonné module.

(i) The previous page asserts that if B lifts A, then the isomorphism H^1_DR(B/Λ) ≅ M⊗_W Λ is canonical and functorial. Here M is the classical Dieudonné module, and Λ is an Artinian local W-algebra via Cohen's structure theorem. This page adds that functoriality automatically gives compatibility with F and V.

(ii) 2.5. Grothendieck admits he has not checked affirmations 1 and 2 but has no doubt they are correct. He then draws the deformation-theoretic consequence. Liftings of A/k to an abelian scheme B over Λ correspond exactly to free rank-g quotients of M⊗_W Λ that reduce mod the maximal ideal to the canonical rank-g quotient of M⊗k = H^1_DR(A). That canonical quotient is H^1(A,O), i.e. the Hodge filtration.

(iii) 3º, the general form. For A/S an abelian scheme there is the Hodge filtration
0 → f_*Ω^1 → H^1_DR(A/S) → R^1f_*O → 0.
For a thickening S ⊂ T and a lift B/T, the crystal value M(T) = DR^1(A/S)(T) = H^1_DR(B/T) receives the Hodge filtration of B. This filtration depends only on the isomorphism class of B and lifts the Hodge filtration of M(S).
- Third affirmation: lifts of A to T correspond bijectively to lifts of the Hodge filtration to a filtration of M(T) with locally free quotients.
- Stronger form: the functor B ↦ (A, φ = Hodge filtration of DR^1(A/S)(T)) is an equivalence of categories, from abelian schemes over T to abelian schemes over S equipped with such a lifted filtration.
This is exactly the Grothendieck–Messing deformation theorem, here in its abelian-scheme form.

(iv) Programmatic remarks. The statement is suggestive for higher-degree de Rham cohomology of smooth projective morphisms, with the Hodge filtration included. That filtration is not crystalline, i.e. not a filtration of the crystal itself. It is a 'continuous' structure whose variation should faithfully reflect the variation of the motive. This is the germ of a p-adic period map / local Torelli, and of the later separation in p-adic Hodge theory between 'crystal plus a separate filtration' (filtered F-crystals, period domains).
errors: Affirmations 1 and 3 are stated for arbitrary nilpotent closed immersions S→T and arbitrary Artinian Λ. In mixed or positive characteristic they are only correct for thickenings with (nilpotent) divided powers, as in Grothendieck–Messing and Berthelot's crystalline site. For a non-PD thickening, e.g. k[t]/(t^p) → k, the de Rham cohomology of a lift is not canonically independent of the lift, and lifts of the filtration do not classify deformations. Grothendieck flags that he has not verified the claims, and the PD condition was incorporated in later work.

'ne dépendant que de la classe à isomorphisme près': for the correspondence to be bijective, the description should be in terms of lifts up to unique isomorphism. Isomorphisms of lifts restricting to the identity on A are unique (rigidity), so this is harmless.

ideas.what: Deformations of an abelian scheme along a nilpotent thickening are classified by lifts of the Hodge filtration in the de Rham/crystalline H^1 evaluated on the thickening; stated as an equivalence of categories.
ideas.modern_name: Grothendieck–Messing deformation theory (abelian schemes / Barsotti–Tate groups)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (ICM Nice 1970, Montréal lectures 1970), Messing (LNM 264, 1972), Mazur–Messing (LNM 370, 1974)
ideas.where_published: Grothendieck, 'Groupes de Barsotti-Tate et cristaux', Actes ICM 1970; 'Groupes de Barsotti-Tate et cristaux de Dieudonné' (Montréal 1974)

ideas.what: Dieudonné module of A over a perfect field equals crystalline/de Rham H^1 of any lift, with F and V induced by Frobenius/Verschiebung.
ideas.modern_name: Crystalline Dieudonné theory; comparison of H^1_cris with the Dieudonné module
ideas.where_published: ICM 1970 talk; Coates–Jussila notes 'Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes' (Dix exposés, 1968)

ideas.what: The Hodge filtration is not crystalline but a 'continuous' structure varying with the motive; suggested generalisation to smooth projective morphisms in higher degree.
ideas.modern_name: p-adic period maps / crystalline local Torelli; filtered (F-)crystals; Griffiths-type variation
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne (K3 liftings, 1981), Ogus (crystalline Torelli), Fontaine, Rapoport–Zink period domains
ideas.where_published: Hinted in the ICM 1970 talk; the letter to Tate itself circulated and is cited in the literature (e.g. Illusie's and Berthelot's historical accounts)

deep.surprise_reason: This is the well-known 1966 letter to Tate in which Grothendieck first formulates crystalline Dieudonné theory and the Hodge-filtration description of deformations. Both are fully developed and credited (Grothendieck–Messing). The 'non-crystalline, continuous' remark anticipates p-adic period maps but is in the spirit of known later work. The text is historically valuable but not new to specialists.
transcription_corrections: The symbol rendered '∅' in 'B ⇝ (A,∅)' and in the handwritten insertion is Grothendieck's letter φ (Ø), naming the filtration, not the empty set.
'DR^1(A/A)(S)' appears so in the typescript (Grothendieck's typo for DR^1(A/S)(S)), so the transcription is faithful.
'Λ' in 'sur Λ' and 'M⊗_W Λ' is typed as an inverted-V caret in the image; the reading Λ is correct.
